soundness_flags.one_line: The detailed jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version is not the standard condition stated in WestlingGilbertCarone2020; retag it novel and justify it as the exact-dose version convention.

soundness_flags.label: ass:p-smooth, ass:g-smooth, ass:m-smooth, ass:r-smooth
soundness_flags.one_line: Calling global fixed-radius C^s smoothness of all four primitives with s>3(d+1) standard under TakatsuWestling2025 misstates that source's much weaker local regularity; this is an instrumental strengthened class and must be retagged novel or weakened.

source_verification_receipts.version: July 2001 author manuscript corresponding to Annals of Statistics 29 (2001), 1699--1731
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies fixed-point monotone LR testing and identifies its universal limit as the integral of squared unconstrained minus constrained Brownian--GCM slopes.
The studied stationary field is the Brownian-parabolic argmax displacement process and its absolute value, with growing-interval extrema; it is not a GCM LR-energy field.
The article gives compound-Poisson exceedance point-process limits for stationary sequences under dependence conditions and characterizes limiting exceedance processes.

source_verification_receipts.version: preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 40 (2012), 1578--1608
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives a Gumbel limit for the supremum-norm error of Grenander-type estimators, at order (n/log n)^(-1/3).

The source defines the observed G-computed curve, gives causal identification under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and positivity, and studies the monotone observed-law model; it does not state the proposal's jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2508.08415, public preprint; JASA DOI 10.1080/01621459.2026.2639735 publication text was not publicly inspectable
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The public theorem summary describes doubly robust LR-type confidence intervals at a fixed continuous-treatment dose, including cross-fitting and flatness adaptation; it does not advertise a simultaneous LR maximum theorem.

The uniform-band theorem assumes twice continuously differentiable theta with Hölder-continuous second derivative and Lipschitz marginal treatment density, rather than global C^s regularity of p, g, m, and r at s>3(d+1).

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the exact-dose potential-mean continuity convention and the high-smoothness primitive class as novel; explain a concrete scientific data-generating regime where each is credible, and separate that justification from the statistical rate argument.

Rework the learner/transfer rung under a materially weaker, literature-facing nuisance condition, or state the high-smoothness result explicitly as a regular-subclass theorem and add a second theorem quantifying the remainder threshold needed for the Gumbel transfer.
Add a numerical worked canonical-field exhibit that computes the Palm-root event, padded maximum, and proposed centering on one finite Brownian grid before claiming practical calibration.
